description: Evaluation metrics of task T042. Every valid row states one dataset, the evaluated outcomes, and the metric sets the Rust core computes: predicted outcome counts, the confusion matrix over the reference categories, and the six contract rates with their numerators, denominators, and values. A null value states one zero denominator. Every invalid row states the reason code and the field path of its rejection.

metadata.name: Evaluation metric cases
metadata.intended_population: Release notes of one product area. No prevalence claim.
metadata.sampling_method: Selected from reviewed development work. No prevalence claim.

valid.note: One pair for every reference category and every predicted outcome that the contracts state, with slices over the record tags. The false acceptance rate and the error among accepted cases share their numerator and state different denominators.
One dataset without any reference label. The review rate and the automatic coverage measure every evaluated case, the label coverage states zero, and the three error rates hold no denominator.

Partial labels. The check reference of one record covers one check alone, so the label coverage differs per scope, and the overall reference of the second record comes from the aggregate of its one check reference.

The two error metrics apart. One reference fail case predicted pass gives both metrics the numerator 1, over the reference fail and review denominator 1 and over the labeled predicted pass denominator 3.
Zero denominators. Every reference states pass and nothing predicts pass, so the false acceptance rate and the error among accepted cases state no value while the false rejection rate states one.

valid.note: Errors and skips over all attempts. The reference fail case that errored and the reference review case that was skipped stay in their denominators, and the totals state attempts, latency with its case count, and usage.

invalid.note: No evaluated case is no evidence: no metric holds one denominator.
One outcome that names no record of the dataset states nothing about that record.
One repeated case identifier counts one case twice.
One outcome that names no check of the definition.
One outcome that omits one check of the definition. Every check is required.
